utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll try to let you go today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zelenika. Mr. Zelenika, do you know -- sorry. By the time you got to the village, you saw that there had been some heavy fighting at the school where the headquarters of the 3rd Battalion of the Rama Brigade was based; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. The fighting was over by the time I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps the question wasn't phrased well. But you became aware that there had been heavy fighting at the school; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that. I saw dead soldiers lying around, but I'm not aware of the nature of the fighting that had gone on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Did you know a soldier by the name of Vlajcic Gusto or Gusto?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was at the communications centre in the school. He's probably better placed to tell you what sort of fighting had gone on because he was there that morning and I was at Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And how well did you know Mr. Vlajcic back at the time of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd known him for a long time. He worked at the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from Kranjcici which is the neighbouring village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you still know him today; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He still works at the school. He's the registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. He's a person with decent education; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And so are you; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sort of, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, there's no one else with the name Gusto Vlajcic in your village or the neighbouring villages, is there?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in my local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Nor is there anyone else with the name Kazo Zelenika in your local area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I understand. Now, you and Mr. Vlajcic both cooperated in the production of a book concerning the deaths at Uzdol, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to show the witness a copy of this book and ask him some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could I just hold up in court first of all a book. Does that appear to you to be the cover of a copy of the book which you and Mr. Vlajcic in company produced? I'll hand it to you to look through by all means if you need to. In fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, would you please inform us about the title of the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The title of the book is "Uzdol." It's a book entitled "Uzdol."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have present in court paper copies. An effort is being made to upload the whole thing into the system. Unfortunately, because a technical misunderstanding yesterday that wasn't able to be done, and I would ask that copies of that book be distributed now. The book itself has English and B/C/S translations in it. But, however, we've noticed that there may be a couple of translation issues as between the two, so that I'm going to get the witness, when I take him to the text, I'll take him to the B/C/S text, and where the B/C/S text departs I will then see if there are any translation issues. Could the witness please be given a copy of that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Can a courtesy copy be provided for the booths too.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 315.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've been requested to -- that a copy be provided to the interpreters and that should be done. I just want to check that we've got one. Very well. Your Honours, I have -- I'll indicate I'm going to cross-examine about certain aspects of this book. I've got an original present which I can tender at the end of all of this. I was going to use it because I've got my notes on it, I was going to use it, but just so that there's no doubt about the book itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what's the number of that book, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is MFI 315.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I indicate, Your Honour, as MFI 315 we're going to upload it. We thought we were going to be able to do it yesterday. That was technical hitch. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. -- Mr. Zelenika, would you just turn to the first page where the credits are to be found. So I'll hold it up and show you the page I want. Not that page but this page. I'm just display to the Court what I'm showing. That page there. Very well. Do you have the page where it says -- it ought to be very early on in the bundle. It will be the third page on the photocopied bundle, the left-hand side of that third page. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, do you have the page which is headed "Sarajevo 9 listopada 2000?" Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To the left of that, do you have a page that lists with the word "izdavac" at the top?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see your name on that page?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you see the name Gusto Vlajcic on that page as well?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And is your page associated with the word "text"?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I may be allowed to clarify something about the book. This book --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just one second, please. I'm going to ask you a lot of questions about this book. I just want to clarify certain contribution situations here. The word "obrada teksta," that's not translated in English here. Could you tell us what's the meaning of "obrada teksta" which is the words associated with Gusto Vlajcic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew these people. I knew when they were born. I had it all in my books. Those were familiar people, neighbours and relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew this basic information on each and every person in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just at this stage I just have to clarify certain of the words there. You see the word "text" above your name, Kazimir Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You see that word "text"? What is the meaning of the word "text" in your understanding?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means writing down the couple of sentences in the lives of those persons, when they were born, where they were born, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this thing, "obrada teksta," text processing, and in case I got something wrong grammatically this person would set the record straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then you have proof-reading which is one level up from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you produced the basic text. Gusto Vlajcic read over that to make sure it was grammatically correct, and then it moved up another level to Dr. don Tomo Vuksic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but not all the persons were there immediately. I didn't know some of the people, so others did their write-ups. There were soldiers who came to be included later, and gradually I did the write-ups for the Uzdol people, those who I knew, but there were a handful of people I didn't know. They wanted their photographs, too. I have no idea how they eventually obtained them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm keep my questions to the Uzdol people, but of course if I ask you about someone, for example, one of the tank drivers or somebody else, then you indicate what you have to say about those. But I want you now, please, to go to page 60, where the photograph on the page 61 is to be found and it's a photograph of Ruza Zelic. Now, just wait for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I want -- I'm going to ask the witness to read out the B/C/S version onto the transcript. That's because the translation below is not certified in any way by the CLSS here, although it's a translation that maybe of use. So I'm going to ask the witness to read that in. The interpreters in the booth now have a courtesy copy but I want to point out that we would like, to the best of their ability, a simultaneous translation as they see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zelenika, would you please read out the -- the -- in Croatian, please, the extract concerning Ruza Zelic, and if you wouldn't mind reading it reasonably slowly so the interpreters can interpret as you go. I mean read it out loud so we can hear it being read.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ruza Zelic, born Dzalto, 25th of" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop, please. I apologise for this, and because it is being interpreted there is a need for you to read very slowly. I'm sorry about that, but it's because it's being interpreted. So would you please do that for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right from the beginning you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ruza Zelic, maiden name Dzalto, born on the 25th of December, 1944 in Uzdol, father Mijo, mother Mara, maiden name Grubesa. Married on the 24th of February, 1965 in Uzdol to Josip Zelic. She and Josip had six children, four sons and two daughters. What can we say about Ruza? A stout woman, corpulent, very sharp but honest. Her Josip was a miner. He worked in many different places in Croatia. He would come home whenever salary had arrived. They built a new house and moved in. They worked hard. Josip suddenly took ill and went to be treated in Split. After a short illness, he died in Split on the 27th of May, 1992. Ruza remained a widow and single mother. The war began. Her son Ivan died on the 24th of January, 1993, at the Uskoplje relay. She was shattered by grief and pain. She lives with her children: Marko, 1978; Marija, 1980; and Stjepan, 1983. She lived with them until her death on the 14th of September, 1993 when Muslim soldiers, members of the BH army. Started shooting near the house. Ruza threw a hand grenade out through the window, fled with the children and ran for some 500 metres down the road where the Muslim soldiers caught up with her, captured her, and killed her by a burst of fire. Little Stjepan was still naked, and he was -- his throat was slit, whereas the daughter Marija was killed by gunfire right there in the middle of the road. May she rest in peace."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. That text is compiled by you; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there -- there are certain changes of that been made. I wrote it down on a slip of paper by hand which they later scanned, whatever, and inserted certain changes to my text. Some of the people who processed the text changed things around. I provided the data, but then they turned things around. As for these data, it's all accurate as far as the year of birth and the year of death is concerned and all the dates, but there are changes that have been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where did you get the information concerning the hand grenade throwing, Mr. Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never got the information. I provided my text. They took it away. I never saw it again. I was given the book later once it had been published. Someone had translated the book into English and German, whatever. I've no idea what changes they made later. I hand wrote my own contribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, your information at the time you hand wrote your contribution --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone -- someone included this hand grenade thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Somebody else has put that in falsely, have they? Is that your account?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Someone added something. Someone added something. Perhaps they knew better than I did. My job was to provide the data, when people were born, when they died, but they added things later on, so that's why there's actually more than I wrote. Some of the things can be translated, I suppose. They said, We made a couple of changes just in order to make the translation process easier. That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But just a moment. Did you point out this mistake that you claim there is about the hand grenade to any person after you saw the book?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The book had already been released. I got a number of copies. Purportedly this book was published to help sponsor the construction of the memorial centre, to contribute funds. The parish priest was in charge, and one over in Sarajevo too. I'm not sure how many copies were eventually printed. I got one. This book was supposed to help raise funds to -- to build this memorial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. But just sticking with the hand grenade for the moment if you don't mind. Is it your suggestion that Gusto Vlajcic added this into the story, about throwing the hand grenade?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no way I can know that. The people kept adding things. I wrote the whole thing down in my office, and I gave the text that I wrote to the parish priest. He may have called Gusto or the other person. I have no idea what his name was. And Tomo Vuksic. I don't know this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Does his title indicate pretty clearly to you that he is an official of the Catholic church, Dr. Don Tomo Vuksic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. He worked with the parish priest. I simply don't know this person, that's what I'm saying. That the book was published in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That may be so --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.000 copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But just again sticking to this detail about the hand grenade, if that's okay. I want to find out who's put that in since you claim it wasn't you. Who else edited this book apart from those who are mentioned in the front of the book as editing it? That's you -- or as contributing to it. That's you and Gusto Vlajcic.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was asked to provide data. There is no way I could have written this myself. He said, Just give us the date of birth, date of death, father's name, mother's name, when these people were married, when the husband died, that sort of thing. We're trying to put together a book and we'll have it published. I'm not sure what the original price was. I think ten German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Never mind the price for the moment. Stick with the hand grenade, please. In terms of the detail of that hand grenade, are you suggesting that the local priest put that into the book?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the front cover of that book -- or the third page which you've looked at already, is there a mention of any other person who was concerned with producing the text of this book apart from you personally?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did the write-ups myself, including the year of birth, that sort of thing. I gave it to the parish priest. I have no idea who else he called. I only saw the book when it came out. There were some photographs too. He had collected photographs from people in the village. There were -- some soldiers were included later on just because at first these soldiers were not included. Some had been mistreated, so they had son included later. So the book actually came out twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Coming back to the hand grenade, if you don't mind. You at the time knew very well that -- that the deceased person Ruza Zelic had hand grenades in her house and was prepared to defend herself while she was still alive?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't know that. I had no idea the woman had actually thrown a hand grenade. I didn't know anything came out the window at all. I had no idea if it had been Ruza or whoever. She was 500 metres further down the road. I had no idea that she had the hand grenade or she was actually able to use it. She was a rather big-boned woman, despite which I had no idea whether she could actually use a hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to that book from time to time. Now, what I have in mind, Mr. Zelenika, is to take you through effectively house by house the walk that you took when you made the sad observations that you saw with your neighbours and relatives and close people killed. Can I indicate when it comes to your family home and what happens there the questions are going to be very, very short and I won't trouble you with them, but I have to ask you some questions about details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P301. That's the map that he -- that was produced in court and was marked by him indicating the houses at Cer and up in Zelenike. I think that might have to be placed on the ELMO, Your Honours, as it was marked yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenika, while that's being done I just indicate that I'm not going to ask you to mark it again. It's just so you can orient the Court and all of us here when I'm asking you questions. I want to take you first of all to the house or to the area where Domin Rajic, Ivo, and Ivko and of course Zerka Glibo were found deceased. Is that the house that you marked with the number 2 there on that drawing?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you raise the image a little bit. Yes, that's house number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, my questions really concern some facts about what you observed here. First of all, what you observed in this case was that all of the deceased were out in the open in the sense that they -- they were not inside the house but outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at the corner of the house, beneath the house, apart from Zerka who was further away near a woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The next question is: To your knowledge, apart from the deceased and those who shot them, do you know of any eyewitnesses to the killing of those people?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Marko, Zoran's -- Zora's husband was there. Marko who was in uniform, or who wore a uniform, he was a home guard. And I think Franjo, Domin's brother was there. I think they had some sort of rifles. They both died of cancer after the war, perhaps in 1998 or 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Franjo and Marko are not people who are named on the indictment here. Both of those are people who were -- who survived the events of Uzdol on the 14th and lived for some time afterwards?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Both of those were people who were of -- who were in uniform on the day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were a member of the home guards. They were guarding Kransko Polje, and they left Kransko Polje. They followed us. But Marko was somewhere there hiding in the woods. He had taken his rifle and fled up above, and he was up there in the woods, and his wife probably started fleeing towards him. He survived and she was killed. He had hidden, and he didn't even dare to shoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And did he gave a statement to your or any authorities about what he saw, if anything?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Quite a few people turned up afterwards and asked questions, but I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you personally didn't speak to him about what he saw; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said shooting started -- what happened, they killed Dominika Ivo. He said, We started fleeing. He said, I couldn't even open fire. He was an elderly man. He was in the vicinity in a -- in the woods. He was crying, sad. It was tragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But the situation -- well, I'll ask you about him and I'll ask you about you. What you saw is that the deceased people were all lying dead near to a young man, that being Ivo, who was uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivo was a soldier. The mother and father were there by him, and Zerka was a little further away, four or five metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But effectively what you had was people killed in the company of an armed and uniform soldier out of doors; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko had already come out of the woods when we arrived there, and that ABiH then returned via Here. He was already there when they arrived, and he was crying, and Domino's brother Franjo was crying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I just want to be clear about the time periods here. You arrived after the killing had stopped as you indicated. Marko and Franjo, were they there when the killing started or did they arrive later?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franjo was in Kransko Polje, but when we went to Cer, when we saw Slavko Mendes there, Franjo ran home. He arrived before I did. Marko was already there. He was there when the shooting broke out. And in Domin's house there was a cafe of some sort. The troops had broken the glass in the cafe. They took something to drink, juices, et cetera. There was some beer there. They then took the bottles and smashed them and set off in the direction of Here. That's what Marko said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's still a cafe there, but it's not open for business.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What I'm getting at here is: Was Marko present when the killings took place?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko had fled to the woods above Domin's house. As to how far away he was I don't know, but he came out before we arrived. He was crying. He said, They've killed my wife. They've killed Domin's daughter. Because he was a refugee there with his wife and they were staying in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now come to the question of Ivo, the soldier. Did you see Ivo's gun when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All I could see is that he had some sort of a bump above his eye, but I can't remember a rifle. I can't remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What you can say about that is that Marko, the survivor, was armed and in uniform at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in uniform, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And armed?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had that rifle. I think Marko had that rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I've got some questions for --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or perhaps he was carrying Ivo's rifle or Franjo's; I don't know. Because Franjo was in Kransko Polje. Then he came down with he is. He had an M-48. I don't know whose rifle it was, but I saw one rifle. Maybe Marko had taken it from someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I've got some questions concerning the deceased Domin who was there. You were asked questions yesterday about Domin and his status in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'd like the witness to be shown a document, please. This is uploaded. This is Defence 65 ter number D1545, and its ERN number is 035639 -- hang on, that's not a Defence number. That's the ERN number. 05 -- sorry, 03563940. I'm sorry. My -- my assistant's not here right at the moment, and I'm just told now this also might not be uploaded. May I just confirm that with the court deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Morrissey. It's not been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is material that was disclosed to the Defence by the Prosecutor under Rule 68, and we have papers copies of it which we'll now -- rather than delaying, we'll distribute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is an official document that I'm going to show you. I'll just ask for your comment on it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May we have a number on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 316.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you look firstly at the first

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you look firstly at the first page of that document, and I just want you to confirm -- I'll ask you first of all whether you've ever seen yourself in your position as registrar, or as a friend and member of the community if you've ever seen that letter it -- yourself personally before.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. But you, nevertheless, are familiar with the system that was put in place by the government to provide financial assistance to those -- to the families of those who fell during the hostilities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they provided some sort of assistance, a bag of flour, things like that. So perhaps that was why he was on the list. Otherwise, he wouldn't have obtained anything. They lived in Uzdol, and Marko and Zora had even been in the house. Here I can see that it says Mr. Pavlovic too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And who was Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, he must have been from Prozor. I don't know. He wasn't in Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. But --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a commander there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, I understand that. But he was an official of the Rama Brigade, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "za," for here. Someone must have signed this on his behalf. I don't know who.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We're had some talk about the word "za." When you say "za," is that short for "zastupa"?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Pavlovic probably didn't sign it. Probably someone else, a deputy, an assistant of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, anyway look, I don't want to -- I'm sorry to distract us there. But could I ask you to go to the next page where there is a certificate, an official certificate saying that Domin Rajic of -- and with certain details, got killed in the Uzdol by the MOS forces at 16 hours on the 14th of the 9th, 1993. He was killed by a bullet. He was performing a task ordered by Commander Josip Prskalo. Do you see that part of the certificate?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But Prskalo didn't sign this. Someone asked for this for a reason, but I don't think Prskalo signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something is not quite clear here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that's okay. Let me just ask you the details about this. Your understanding is that the government did in fact give some assistance of a limited kind to the family of Domin Rajic arising from the facts set out in these letters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the government but our warehouse from Prozor --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- provided assistance for the troops. And then they had to provide the civilians who lived in the places with some sort of assistance in the form of flour, tins, cold meat, et cetera. That was the form the assistance took.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. But what I'm talking to your about now is that these documents indicate clearly, don't they, that Domin was mobilised in the HVO and that upon his death assistance was rendered to the family or was authorised to be rendered to the family because he was performing a task ordered by Commander Josip Prskalo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You know the -- are you aware of a ministry called the Ministry of Defenders of the Herzegovina Neretva Canton?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very familiar with that, but -- there are various sorts of organisations, but as to their names, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, anyway, you don't dispute, do you, that in fact now that you think about it, Domin Rajic was mobilised as a soldier in the home guard of the Rama Brigade at the time he was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I offer that document for tender. Not on the basis that this witness has seen it, but on the basis that it's an official document. Its of chain of custody we think can be proved very thoroughly, and it was given to us by the Prosecutors, so I offer it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I offered the book or whether the book was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. It's been --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's been marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- marked, but you did not offer it. Maybe you could save it until --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's what I had in mind, Your Honour. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I apologise that these questions have to go into some detail but it's important we do it as thoroughly as we can. Very well. The next house that I want to ask you about is marked as number 3, and there were found the deceased Kata and Mato Ljubic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Kata Ljubic was your godmother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: She joined the HVO; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: She worked as a cook. She baked bread initially until we had the possibility of obtaining real bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But whatever capacity you say she was working in, whether it be as cook or anything else, the fact is she did join the HVO, didn't she? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's what they say. If that's a member, she was a member. She didn't have a uniform. She didn't have a weapon. They'd bring in a tonne of flour and they would have to bake the bread, all elderly women. But Kata was there, and there were other women baking the bread too. Ivka baked bread too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would -- would the witness just have regard to that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you mind just looking back at the book.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 315.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 315. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right you have -- do you still have your copy of the back there, Mr. Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll -- I'll leave that with you because I'm going to ask you various questions about that book so even when I'm not questioning I don't mind if you keep possession of that book. Now, on page 64 -- would you mind going to page 64.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I think it's --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kata Ljubic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's right. Page --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, we just want to make sure we've got the -- would you mind just holding up the page that you've got in front of you so I can be sure as to whether I'm directing you wrongly. Would you mind just holding it up so I can see it. Sorry. Well, yes, that's the page. Do you see above --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see a picture of Kata Ljubic and above the photograph the page number 65?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I just want to ask you about the text there, Kata Ljubic. I won't get to your read out the whole thing. But is it the fact that that text says that at the outbreak of the home defending war Kata immediately joins the HVO as does her husband Ivan. She works in the kitchen and is famous for her "pogaca," which is a particular bread. Do you see that section there?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The bread, that's what she did initially. But perhaps the army knows when we started receiving already-baked bread. Because initially the flour would arrive, and there were problems. When we started receiving new bread Kata was no longer involved, but what it says about her over there, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Her husband Ivan was a home guard, a member of the home guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, look, I'll come to all that in just a moment. But at the moment that -- the information that's contained in that passage there, in that passage of text, is accurate information to your knowledge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that's information that you provided as --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't know -- perhaps I wrote this, but I didn't write the date up until which she was there because she was there at the beginning. She helped us, and I thank her for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Zelenika, can I just make it clear none of the questions I'm asking are designed to insult or put any aspersions upon the deceased, but I have to press you with these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Defence Exhibit D1544. That is in the same category as the previous one. It's another similar document to the one I just tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenika, what's about to be shown to your is a very similar document to the one I showed you about Domin Rajic. This is document concerning HVO membership of Kata, and I just ask you to look at this, if you don't mind, and I'll ask you similar questions to the ones I asked concerning -- concerning Domin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Does it appear --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Morrissey. That's will be MFI 317.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you have a document in front of you a certificate about -- which is -- a document headed certificate about the circumstances of the killing. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And does that document say that -- that Kata Ljubic was a member of the Rama Brigade from the 3rd of the 4th, 1992 until the 14th of the 9th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And at the bottom does it say that Kata Ljubic was killed by -- killed under the circumstances that during the attack of MOS forces against Uzdol while carrying out the order on the Defence front line. Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it, but I don't know what it is. I don't know who wrote such nonsense down here, and I don't know why this was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's just that you're here and I have to put these documents to you. First of all, have you ever seen this document before now?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And secondly, you're familiar, though, with the -- with the system of granting relief to the families of those killed in the war as you've already indicated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with that, and there's -- there are a lot of people who are receiving assistance, and there are others who don't receive any assistance although they should be receiving such assistance. Those in the HVO and the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I offer that document for tender as well, even though he hasn't seen it on the same basis as the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And now I have some questions about the killings of Mato and Kata. First of all, at the time did anyone tell you that they were an eyewitness to the actual killing of those two people?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one did. Below the house Kata was -- waved to us. She started fleeing. She said, Flee Mato, run. She started running down towards the church, towards her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But who saw this take place to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko saw this, Marko who was there. He said Kata was there and Ivka and Zora, and then Kata and Marko started fleeing. They said, Run, they're shooting. She entered the house. That's why she didn't -- she wasn't killed where they were killed. She entered the house from one side and she was found on another side. She started fleeing towards the church and that's where she was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you refer to Marko, is that the same Marko who was present at the other house that we were talking about before where Domin and Ivo --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Marko. Marko and Zora were at her house. Later the shooting broke out. She fled to her house and they remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. And -- now, you've mentioned that her son -- sorry, pardon me. I take that back. Apart from Mato and Kata, who else lived at that house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan was there, too, the husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And was Ivan an HVO soldier?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan was member of the home guard. He was a home guard at Kransko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And was Ivan present at the time when the killings took place or was he somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at Kransko Polje that morning and then he followed us there. He said, Kume, Kume, my house is on fire. He didn't even know that people had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you notice whether Mato had a gun or not when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The house was on fire. There was lots of black smoke all over the place. There was a concrete slab just outside the entrance, and he was over there so I couldn't see. There was so much smoke. There was no clear line of sight. I don't know. But Mato didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you say he didn't have one, did you mean he didn't have one when you saw him or that he didn't own a gun?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't have one. His son Ivan had been at Kransko Polje that morning, and he later joined us, but they did not have any other rifles in their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move on to the next house now, and this one is at -- you've marked it as number 4. That is where Kata Perkovic was killed. Are you aware of any eyewitness --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kata Perkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Are you aware of any eyewitness to that killing?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Letter husband Stipo was there. Later he went to see his son in later in Dubrovnik, and he died two or three years after she had died. He was quite old actually. He was born in 1916. He died in Dubrovnik and later was buried in Uzdol. The village cemetery not in the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. Now, Stipo was present at the time of the killing. Did he see the killing with his own eyes or was he taking shelter in a cupboard somewhere.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there. It was an old house, two rooms. He was in the other room. I've no idea how it was that they didn't kill him. He just -- he was totally beside himself when I found him. He didn't even realise what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you saying that he didn't realise that Kata had been killed yet or not?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was scared to death. He didn't even see his wife. He walked out in front of the house. There was a wooden bench there. He just sat down right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I now want to move towards the village of Zelenike and take you to the -- to the death of Mara Grubesa. Now, at that time when she -- when she died in the barn, her daughter Janja was present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Janja was back home with her and the granny, Mara's mother, Milica Zelic. She was over there in the same place as Ruza 100 metres to the left. She's the mother-in-law but they didn't live together. She came down to see her daughter. Milica made it, Janja made it, and they're in Prozor now. But Milica died in Travnik. She was mentally ill, and she died in a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. How did she get away? Did she run away or was she found hiding at the house? And that's Milica I'm talking about here.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milica probably one day she was in the house. And then Mara left the house to release the livestock. Janja probably followed, but someone called her name out, one of the soldiers, and when she realised that those were no HVO soldiers, she started running. There's a plum tree, an orchard further down the hill. Someone fired at her. She was wounded in one of her hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Janja just ran, paying no heed to her mother. She just ran as fast as she could towards Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We'll ask Janja questions about that in due course, and I understand you weren't there. But I do want to you ask this: At the time when you --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She knows that much better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly. Okay. But I just want to ask you: At the time when you arrived and you spoke to Janja, she didn't --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw Janja the next day. She'd escaped to Prozor and we stuck around that day. So it was not until three or four days after that I saw her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just one second, please. Yes, okay. Well, I just -- the only question I have for you about that topic is: What did -- what did Janja tell you about her observations concerning her mother? Did she see her mother go into the cowshed? Did she hear her mother in the cowshed? Did she even know her mother was in the cowshed, or was she desperately wanting to find out what had happened?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was on her way to release the stock from the cowshed and she did. I'm not sure if their livestock survived. She cut them loose and let them out. The cowshed was burnt to the ground there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mara Grubesa's house was Pavo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pavo, yes. Pavo was also a home guard member at Kransko Polje, alongside with Ivan and Franjo. He came with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So Pavo was a person who had a weapon; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he was at Kransko Polje that morning, Franjo, and he and others. Once we had passed them, they decided to join us and go back with us to see if the rest were still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And Janja who survived was herself an HVO member; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in our kitchen. She was a cook. She was there all the time. Well, I mean, they took shifts, two or three a day, but she was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But specifically speaking, she was a member of the HVO, wasn't she, regardless of the duties that she performed?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. They just helped out at the kitchen. I'm not sure what exactly their official status was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we could assist by going back to the book. If you wouldn't mind just looking at page 56 of the book, the entry under Mara Grubesa. There's a reference to Janja at the bottom of the -- in the last couple of lines there.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see that reference there to Mara's daughter, Janja, the HVO chef? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A cook, HVO. Of course. I mean, she wasn't with the BH army, that's for sure. She worked at the kitchen, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. I understand that. All right. Before I go on to the other houses, I've just got another question for you, a more general one, and then I'm going to resume to those houses. The people -- the commander, Mr. Prskalo who was the battalion commander in the school, he must have been aware at all times that between his command post and the front line there were villages or hamlets which had a mixture of civilians and HVO soldiers living in them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're asking this witness to indicate what Mr. Prskalo -- what was on Mr. Prskalo's mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, unless there is some basis for that, it's purely speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It was well known to you who were a member of the HVO -- sorry, I'll ask the question and then you can answer it. It was well known to your as an HVO member that between the nerve centre of the battalion, the battalion command and the front line, there were villages there were filled with a mixture of civilians and soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were soldiers who were staying with their parents in their homes. When they were off duty, they'd be at their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But when they stayed with their parents in their homes, they were armed and in uniform, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all the time. There was no reason to change. The soldiers didn't wear civilian clothes at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. But in addition to that -- to the soldiers and the civilians, there were also home guard members who were armed and sometimes in uniform and sometimes not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The home guards wore a different kind of uniform. They weren't as good. They looked a little uglier, but perhaps they were warmer than the regular soldiers' uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And sometimes it happened that civilians not in military uniform at all would carry weapons when they were going out of doors to look after their stock and to do their jobs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as a person who participated in the military, you know that in any offensive attack on a local level one of the targets of attackers is going to be the headquarters of the local unit, and in this concrete case any attack in your part of the front was probably going to involve an attack on the school; correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ever point out to Commander Prskalo or anyone else that by having the front line arranged as it was he was placing the civilians as well as the soldiers in grave danger of death in combat?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was a very low-ranking officer, and I can't say anything on behalf of the high-ranking officers. Besides, you had to obey their orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course you did, I understand that. But my question is: Did you ever point it out to them that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. Number one, that's outside the scope of this person's knowledge, number one. This is an expert -- you're asking for an expert opinion. You're also asking technically for a legal opinion because any soldier knows or should know the laws of war and know what the difference between civilians and military targets and who and what you can attack. So this is well outside the scope of this witness's expertise and knowledge. And this is a crime base witness, not a witness they should be asking questions of opinions for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that this question is just a general question, and the Defence will not ask any further questions concerning any specific military expertise. This question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I confirm that's right, that I won't be asking him for any expert opinions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. So the question was I understand that you were of a lower rank and you had to obey orders, but did you ever point out that danger to your superiors yourself?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That would have been out of place, and they wouldn't have listened. Those were young people who did things their own way. What was I supposed to tell them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not criticising you about it, I'm asking you and you've begin your answer. That's okay. I want to move on to the next house, and the next one is -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe we could have a break since you are going to another section.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will take a break and we will resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Zelenika. I want to continue around the -- the path that you took now, and I want to move to the deceased Dragica Zelenika. Are you aware of any eyewitness to the killing of Dragica?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The person Marko that you referred to who had escaped before, what was Marko's full name?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko Glibo. Marko Glibo, an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Can you indicate how old Marko Glibo was at that time approximately?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was born in 1938, possibly 1939.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Do you recall whether he was a person who wore glasses or not?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll proceed now -- we'll proceed now with respect to Dragica. Now, when you came to see the condition she was in, she had -- her body had been significantly burnt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The house had burned down too. It appears that some of the beams and roof tiles had crashed on top of her, and she was in a very bad state when we found her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did it appear to your that lying in the position that she was when you saw her that her body must have been removed from the immediate vicinity of the fire?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I just passed by in a hurry on my way to join the rest of the group. Her body was lying there black, and the house had burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did she have a son? Did she have number of sons?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Her husband had died before the war. He used to work as a paramedic in Uzdol. He died before the war, and yes, she did have a number of sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were any of those sons HVO members?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One was with the police, and the rest were with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Were any resident in Uzdol at this time?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One or two. Ante, Mile was in Prozor. I'm really not sure. I think Ante was resident. He was the youngest son.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How old was Ante?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 something, 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Ante at the time when these killings took place?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He may have been at the front line. He may have been back home. I can't say. Or perhaps he was off duty on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it's very possible that he slept the night before in the house with Dragica and was there when the shooting started; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea where he'd spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Again I have a general question stepping outside of the individual deceased. I'll come back to those, of course. But you heard of a number of -- of HVO soldiers who were in uniform and armed who fled from those villages. I'll give you some examples. Ivka Stojanovic's son is one. Ivan Kovcalija is another. But generally speaking, you were aware, weren't you, of that fact?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People fled. Fabjan Ratkic did. Janko fled. Even Kovcalija survived. Janja survived too. There were some other women who had fled. Andja Zelenika was a boy named Milan or Marko. He was Pero Dzanko's son. He survived too, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And it's quite obvious to you as well that a number of the killed persons whose bodies you saw were killed outside of their homes.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were inside and some were outside near their homes, 20, 30 metres, depending. Some were killed on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. All right. Well, I'll return to the specifics now. I have a couple of questions about your own home. I'm not going to ask you about the specifics about what you saw there, but I'll limit the questions to this: When you found your father, he was not in his bed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was on the floor, on the carpet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And you've indicated already that -- well, perhaps I should ask you this: You indicated that your father and you also had been hunters and members of a hunting club. I take it, therefore, that you had firearms in the house.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. The 16-millimetre rifle, two barrelled, double barrelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. Did you see that rifle on that day?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll move on to the next --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We still have the rifle, but I don't remember having seen it on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it's come into your possession since that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And now I want to move on to the Ruza Zelic and the two children there. Are you aware of any eyewitness to the killing of those three?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no eyewitness. They were at the far end of the village. They tried to run further down, and they were killed on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please have on the ELMO made available to him the map that he drew which is actually still sitting there on the ELMO right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now on the screen in front you there may be the map that you drew. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. On that map at the very right-hand edge you've indicated where the Zelic house is, and then nearby you've indicated where the bodies of the three were found. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you able to indicate whereabouts in relation to the bodies and the house whereabouts Stipo's tracksuit pants were found?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the old house. There's a path past the house, and it was five metres further down, this low black shrub there, and the tracksuit pant, dark blue, was hanging off the shrub, and their bodies were found 300 or 400 metres further down the road. That's where they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So just to be clear about that, if you went to the Zelic's -- if you -- if you were in the Zelic's house and you walked out of their house towards where the bodies were found, the Zelic children and mother, would you pass by that pair of black -- that pair of -- I'm sorry, I've started to speak and am stumbling away. I will start again. If you position yourself in the Zelic's house and then walk in the direction towards where the bodies were found, do you pass by in the course of that walk the tracksuit pants?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First we reached her house, and while we were on that path -- it's not really a road, it's a sort of village path that tractors can use, from that path we saw Stipo's tracksuit. I knew it. And then as we looked at the tracksuit, we descended. We -- there was a meadow to the left. We descended to the path where the path forks off towards my house. One road goes to Here and another to the school, and at the crossroads the road forks off towards my house, and they were killed on that road that goes towards my house. They were killed down below to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to proceed a little further with that, in relation to those tracksuit pants, where were found the pieces of military equipment that you've given evidence about? You remember there was talk about a magazine for a gun and so on. How far from the tracksuit pants were they?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were found in the vicinity of the people who had been killed. Twenty or 30 metres above them there's a sort of area, a sort of borderline area. That's where this was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. I must have misunderstood. So these items were found near to the bodies, not near to the tracksuit pants. That the position?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the bodies. Down below in the meadow, the thicket.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could I ask you to look at the book, please, at page 91 of the book. It's the entry on Marija. Do you have that entry? Okay. I won't get you to read the whole thing out there, but I will ask you this: Does the entry there say that on the 14th of September, at daybreak, while still asleep they are awakened by machine-gun bursts and shots fired by Muslim soldiers, member of the BiH army. Their mother Ruza, surrounded by Muslim soldiers, tosses a hand grenade out of her window, jumps with her children Marija and Stjepan out of another window and runs towards the road looking for rescue. They run for about 500 metres until they meet the road where the Muslim soldiers, members of the BiH army, catch up with them, and then gives details of the death. Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Where does the information come from that was included in that book and, in particular, that entry?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was written later on. I don't know. Anyone might say that she threw it or that the army did, that the little child was killed. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what you say to this Tribunal is that you didn't write that entry yourself or that part of the entry yourself. Is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wrote this part above, but perhaps something has been amended, changed here, added, I don't know. There must have been an autopsy, because when you see dead bodies, you can't really look at them for very long, and it's a difficult situation. They're all rigid. The book was written later on. People might have said various things. Books are written after the events when they wanted to establish a centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that, and -- but just going back to the hand grenade issue, what you say is you don't know how that hand grenade story got to be included in that book. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. The grenade was thrown as a whole in front of the window, but as to who threw the grenade, who knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I now want to move on to the next series of deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And with respect to these, could the witness please be shown the second of the maps. It is the one labelled B. The previous one was P301, and I think the next one is P303, from memory.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Morrissey. It's P303.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be given that one on the ELMO in the same way as he's had the last on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We're now moving to the second of your three diagrams. The first person I want to ask you about is Ante Stojanovic, Brko, and what you know about that. Firstly with respect to Ante, were you aware or are you aware of any eyewitness to the moment of his death?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. He was found dead ten or 20 metres from the house. He wasn't even wearing any footwear. He was killed in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at the time you saw him, did he have a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was just wearing some sort of a jumper, and I think he had thick socks on. He was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anica was killed in the vicinity of the house on the road. She was wearing some sort of multicoloured dress. Her head was facing downwards. That's what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the death of Anica, are you aware of any eyewitness who witnessed the moment of her death?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When she was killed, a son of hers saw her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was called Ivan Stojanovic, a small child. Ivan. There were several of them. One of them was there. He survived, and I think that he now lives in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. How old was Ivan at the time of this?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 13 or 14 years old. I don't know. It was a young child. I don't remember the year of his birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. You indicated at an earlier time that some young boys -- some teenage boys had a role to play in the defence of the village or in some -- having some function in that regard. What part, if any, were young teenage boys given in the defence of the village to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they weren't boys. I said that these soldiers, they were a lot younger than we were. It was difficult for them to listen to us who were older than they were. They were fearless youths, urchins. They would say, If you're afraid, run to Prozor. Go on. They weren't children. They were soldiers who had been members of the former JNA. They were young, and he was a commander or deputy commander or something like that. But as they say, they didn't pay much attention to people who were older than they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand what you say about that. Do you recall whether Ivan was present on the day -- sorry, you've indicated that he was present on the day that his mother was killed. He was in fact a member of the HVO, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was a child. He was young. He was a child. He wasn't a member of the army. He was a boy living there with his mother. His brother Mato was an HVO soldier who was up in Borak that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. How far away is Borak?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Borak is the first hill from Kriz between Here and Krstiste. Then there's Borak. It's a hill between Kriz and Pale, and then you have Krstiste and Bobari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just so the Tribunal understands, how many metres -- approximately how many metres away from Anica Stojanovic's house was her son Mato when he was up at Borak? Is it a matter of 200 metres or 700 metres or 1.000 metres or how far away?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 1.000 metres. The upper side of Borak is a kilometre and a bit away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was there any artillery of the HVO positioned at Borak?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was in the vicinity of the army lines. I don't know. Perhaps they would occasionally deploy something up there, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware of whether or not the young boy who escaped, Ivan, whether he was armed?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He was a child.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But he was a child living on a -- in a farmhouse in a rural area, so I want to persist with the question. Did they have a hunting weapon in their house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. His father was in Austria. Only his sister had remained and that brother Marko and his mother. I don't know. I don't think they had a hunting rifle because Pero had -- Pero, the father, had about working in Austria for 20 or 30 years. He was suffering from some sort of stress.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Mato, after he'd been in the army, he survived. He married, and he lives in Zagreb with his wife. I think he has a child. And the little boy is now in Zagreb too. He's now a young man. Now he's 25 or 27. At the time he was 14 or 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But you don't rule out the possibility that the HVO brother Mato had left a gun behind in the house in case anything went wrong or in case an attack happened, do you?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't have left it there since he had to have a rifle at the front line. And that morning he was in Borak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I now want to move on to the Ratkices that you've indicated. You indicated yesterday that the two Ratkices that you found were found in the basement of a building --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Blaz's house. His house burnt down. It was a big house, and it burnt down to the ground. It's now been rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. And you clarified that very well for us yesterday. But in terms of how the bodies were why positioned, it was your perception when you first saw them that they'd been thrown down into that basement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the basement they didn't seem to be sitting or lying down. It seemed as if they'd been thrown into the basement. This was a basement in which they would place potatoes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. Very well. Now, with respect to Kata and - excuse me, I'm sorry - and her Martin, is it the fact that they had a son who was present at the time when they were killed or at least in the moments around that time?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a son Fabjan, who lived with them, but I don't know whether Fabjan was in Borak or in the village that morning. I don't know whether he was on leave or whether he was at the line. But Borak also fell, and then they also fled from Borak too. As to whether he was at the front line or in the house, I don't know.
