utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Do you remember having seen any blood on the ground under the bodies of the people who had been killed or in the vicinity of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. There was blood on the ground, in the corridor in my house. As for the bodies outside, I don't know. It was -- there was a lot of earth there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you couldn't say that you noticed traces of blood on the ground where the bodies were?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was blood on their clothes, on their necks. It depended on where they had been hit. There was blood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On their bodies and on their clothes?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was terrible to observe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I understand. And you said that you also saw bodies of members of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was this, roughly speaking? Where were these bodies?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw one on the road to the church and the school at the point where the road forks. There was a house there, and he was between two houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You said that you assumed it was inconceivable, impossible that the HVO would shell its people, but I believe that you also said that you took to the road once the shelling had ceased and once the shooting had ceased. So my question is: What was the HVO shelling and where?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO was shelling the Kransko hill, the highest hill above the village and the hill above Here. Krstiste, that's what the lines are called over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the village itself you didn't notice anything? No shelling?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a stable that had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But you said that outside a certain house there were traces that might have been the traces of a shell. Could that have been the trace of a mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We found a piece of shrapnel from a grenade. There was the -- the handle, the -- under the window by the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But that could not have been a mortar shell, for example.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because there was a piece of it. There was the pin that had remained there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: In your opinion, did the people who were -- carried out the attack attack the school primarily? Was the school the primary objective? Was that your impression? Do you feel that the objective of the attack was something else, not the school?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school was the last target to be attacked, because Kriz and Zelenike had first been set on fire. These villages were already burning before they attacked the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So how did you -- who said that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers who survived in the school because there were soldiers in the school who hadn't been killed. They survived and they were fighting there. Some had been killed, others survived. They said that they saw that Kriz and Zelenike were on fire. And then they came down to the centre because Cer is the sort of centre in our area, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the bodies of the HVO soldiers who had been killed were outside the school, not inside the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on a -- in an area that was flat. I didn't even go to look at them. I went up to my house. When I returned, they had already brought them into the school. They had put them on the tables in the school, and then they took the soldiers to Prozor. And we took the clothes off the civilians and put them in a big lorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of the Judge's questions? I see none. At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. There's MFI 315, 316, and 318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please indicate what kind of document are these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 315 is the book. The book. 316 is, I think, admitted into evidence already, but I know -- perhaps we had made a mistake about that. We thought it had been. But you recall there were two documents, 316 and 317. They were the two pension documents effectively concerning membership of the HVO. If it is the fact that 316 hasn't been admitted, I would move that it be admitted. It may be that we thought it was but we were wrong. And then finally 318 is the series of combat reports which I showed to the witness. There's four of them all bundled together. I think there was no objection to any taken except for that last lot, and I think we put that off until now. Your Honours, if -- if objection is taken to them, then I will defer. I do seek to tender them now, but if objection is taken it would be proper to uphold the objection frankly because this witness didn't see it. There might be other witnesses who -- the Prosecution might take the view that it's okay to tender them. So we better see what they say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Those two documents, 315 and 318, are admitted into evidence. As for the documents 316 and 317, they have already been admitted into the evidence. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We wish you a pleasant journey back home, and after we have adjourn the hearing, Madam Usher will show you out of the room. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of April, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
